item.title: Good Locally Testable Codes
item.description: An explicit construction of locally testable codes of constant rate, constant distance and constant number of queries is given. Hence answering affirmatively the $c^3$-problem. roblem.

item.title: A new approach to strong convergence
item.description: A family of random matrices $\mathbf{X}^N=(X_1^N,\dots,X_d^N)$ is said to converge strongly to a family of bounded operators $\mathbf{x}=(x_1,\dots,x_d)$ when $\Vert P(\mathbf{X}^N,\mathbf{X}^{N\ast})\Vert \to \Vert P(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{x}^*)\Vert$ for every noncommutative polynomial $P$. item.title: A counterexample to Viterbo’s conjecture
item.description: We present a counterexample to Viterbo’s volume-capacity conjecture. This implies, in particular, that in contrast with a well-known conjecture, symplectic capacities do not coincide on the class of convex domains in the classical phase space.

item.title: New large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials
item.description: We prove new bounds for how often Dirichlet polynomials can take large values. item.title: Nash blowup fails to resolve singularities in dimensions four and higher
item.description: In this paper we show that iterating Nash blowups or normalized Nash blowups does not resolve the singularities of algebraic varieties of dimension four or higher over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic.

item.title: Multislicing and effective equidistribution for random walks on some homogeneous spaces
item.description: We consider a random walk on a homogeneous space $G/\Lambda$ where $G$ is $\mathrm{SO}(2,1)$ or $\mathrm{SO}(3,1)$ and $\Lambda$ is a lattice. The walk is driven by a probability measure $\mu$ on $G$ whose support generates a Zariski-dense subgroup. We show … Continue reading →

item.title: Unknotting number is not additive under connected sum
item.description: We give the first examples of a pair of knots $K_1$, $K_2$ in the 3-sphere for which their unknotting numbers satisfy $u(K_1\#K_2)< u(K_1) +u(K_2)$. This answers question 1.69(B) from Kirby’s problem list, in the negative.
